mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 3.0% compresses equity discount rates, increasing present value of future cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 3.0% for 12 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of those periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate decline exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals labor market tightening, which typically precedes corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE declines > 0.2pp but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of subsequent periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and retail sales signals robust consumer demand, which typically leads to higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both increase in the same month but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of those months.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production signals manufacturing slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of those periods.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.5% indicates expanding economic activity, which typically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of subsequent periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate above 3.5% triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5% but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of subsequent periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in non-farm payrolls and decline in unemployment rate signals labor market strength, which typically precedes higher consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases in the same month but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of those months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts during late-cycle expansions signal overheating and potential policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST increases during late-cycle expansions but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of those periods.
